title: Getting started
text: bearings turns a folder of plain markdown guides into a static site. You write the guides, list them in a manifest, and write a layout that gives the site its look. bearings builds the pages, a markdown copy of every guide, llms.txt, a search index and a sitemap, and checks that the links, anchors, code examples, constant names, images and diagrams in them are all sound. It has no theme. The layout is yours: an ERB template your repo keeps beside the manifest.

title: Getting started
heading: Install
text: bearings needs Ruby 3.3 or later. Add it to your Gemfile, with rake, which runs its tasks: group :development do gem 'bearings' gem 'rake' # Only for the constant check, which compares the guides with your RBS signatures. gem 'rbs' end bearings’ own dependencies are kramdown, kramdown-parser-gfm, rouge and zeitwerk. It never needs Node or another program.

title: Getting started
heading: The two Rakefile lines
text: require 'bearings/rake' Bearings::Rake.install That adds four tasks: Task What it does rake docs Builds the site into _site/ rake docs:check Builds the site and runs every check, failing on any error rake docs:serve Builds the site, serves it at http://localhost:8000 and rebuilds it when its files change rake docs:check:external Requests every external link in the guides and reports the ones that fail docs, docs:check and docs:check:external print the problems they found, and exit with status 1 if any is an error. Set FORMAT=json to print them as JSON instead; The checks shows both forms. The manifest is docs-site/manifest.yml unless you pass another path. The layout, the landing page and the site’s other files are read from the manifest’s folder, whatever it is called: Bearings::Rake.install(manifest: 'site/manifest.yml') Every task runs from the repo root, and the ones that build write to _site/ there, so add _site/ to your .gitignore.

title: Getting started
heading: A first site
text:
A site needs a guide, a manifest that lists it, a layout and a landing page: docs/GETTING_STARTED.md docs-site/manifest.yml docs-site/layout.html.erb docs-site/index.html.erb The guide is plain markdown. Its first # line is the page title: # Getting started Install the gem, then run it. The manifest names the site and lists every page, each with the guide it comes from, the slug its URL is built from, and a one-line description: site: name: My gem url: https://docs.example.com watch: - docs groups: - label: Start here pages: - source: docs/GETTING_STARTED.md slug: getting-started description: Install the gem and run it The layout renders each guide. This one is about as small as a layout can be: <%= page.title %> · <%= site.name %>
<%= body %>
The landing page becomes /index.html. It gets the site and its pages, but no single page: <%= site.name %> <%- pages.each do |page| -%>

<%= page.title %>: <%= page.description %>

<%- end -%> Then build and check it: bundle exec rake docs:check The guide is now at _site/guides/getting-started/index.html, with its markdown copy at _site/guides/getting-started.md. Run bundle exec rake docs:serve and open http://localhost:8000 to read it. Note The guide is still a plain markdown file that GitHub renders on its own. Nothing in it is written for bearings: no front matter, no shortcodes, no syntax GitHub would show as text. Relative links between guides, relative image paths, alert blocks like this one and Mermaid diagrams all read the same in both places.

title: Getting started
heading: How a build runs
text: Each build starts the same way. The manifest and the guides it lists become one site model; each output turns that model into files, and each check turns it into problems. flowchart LR accTitle: How a build runs accDescr: The manifest, guides and images become a site model. Outputs turn it into files, which are written to _site. Checks turn it into problems, which go into one report. sources["manifest, guides and images"] --> model["site model"] model --> outputs["outputs"] --> writer["_site/"] model --> checks["checks"] --> report["report"] A run reports every problem it finds, not only the first. rake docs and rake docs:check write _site/ even when they report errors, so you can look at what is wrong; they write nothing only when the manifest itself can’t be read, or two outputs would write the same file. rake docs:serve is the exception: a rebuild with an error keeps serving the last good site. Each build replaces _site/: a file the build no longer writes is deleted, so keep nothing of your own in it.

title: Getting started
heading: Where to next
text: The manifest: every key it takes The layout: what your templates are given Diagrams and images: drawing and showing things in a guide The outputs and The checks: everything a build writes and reports

title: The manifest
text: The manifest is the only list of what the site holds. A guide is on the site because a page in the manifest names it, never because of the folder it is in, and guides carry no front matter: everything bearings knows about a page that is not in the guide itself is here. It lives at docs-site/manifest.yml unless you pass another path to Bearings::Rake.install(manifest:). Every file path in it is relative to the repo root.

title: The manifest
heading: A full manifest
text: This one uses every key: site: name: My gem summary: What my gem does, in one line. url: https://docs.example.com repo: https://github.com/me/my_gem version: lib/my_gem/version.rb namespaces: - MyGem watch: - docs redirects: /guides/setup/: /guides/getting-started/ outputs: llms_full: true checks: image_limit_kb: 200 external_links: false groups: - label: Start here tone: teal pages: - source: docs/GETTING_STARTED.md slug: getting-started featured: true description: Install the gem and run it - source: docs/reference/CONFIGURATION.md slug: reference/configuration description: Every setting and its default Only site.name and groups are required. bearings’ own manifest is docs-site/manifest.yml in its repo.

title: The manifest
heading: site
text: Key Value Default What it does name text The site’s name: the title of llms.txt, and site.name in the layout. Required. summary text none One line about the site, quoted under the title of llms.txt. url text none The address the site is published at. Without it there is no llms.txt, sitemap.xml or robots.txt, and pages have no canonical URL. repo text none The repo’s web address. Each page’s edit_url is <repo>/edit/main/<source>. version text none The path of a file that sets VERSION = '…'. Its value is version in the layout; a file that sets none is a version problem. namespaces list of text none The constants the constant check looks for. Without any, it doesn’t run. The url also changes the markdown copies: an image in a copy points at its full URL on the site, so the copy still shows it when read on its own.

title: The manifest
heading: groups
text: The site’s pages, in reading order, in labelled groups. The order here is the order of the layout’s navigation, of the previous and next links, of llms.txt and of llms-full.txt. A group takes: Key Value What it does label text The group’s heading. Required. pages list of pages The group’s pages, in order. Required. A page takes: Key Value Default What it does source text The guide’s path from the repo root, in any folder. Required, and unique. slug text The page’s URL is /guides/<slug>/. Lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, with / between segments. Required, and unique. description text none One line about the page, for the layout and llms.txt. The description check requires it. featured true or false false A flag for the layout, which might show the page first or larger. bearings does nothing else with it. The page’s title is not in the manifest: it is the guide’s first # line. Pages are numbered 01, 02 and so on, in manifest order, counting separately for each folder their guides are in. The layout gets the number as page.num. Any other key on a group or a page is kept as it is and handed to the layout in extras, so a site can carry details of its own: the tone: teal above is group.extras['tone'].

title: The manifest
heading: watch
text: A list of folders. Every markdown file in them must be a page in the manifest, and every image in them must be shown by a guide; rake docs:check reports the ones that aren’t. Without watch, a guide nobody listed goes unnoticed.

title: The manifest
heading: redirects
text: A mapping of old path to new path, for a URL the site no longer has: redirects: /guides/setup/: /guides/getting-started/ /guides/old-name/: /guides/new-name/#a-heading Each one writes a page at the old path that sends the browser to the new one. The new path must be a page or a file the site writes, and the old one must not be; The checks lists what is reported when they are wrong.

title: The manifest
heading: outputs
text: Key Value Default What it does llms_full true or false false Also writes /llms-full.txt, every guide’s markdown copy in one file.

title: The manifest
heading: checks
text: Key Value Default What it does image_limit_kb a whole number 300 The largest an image a guide shows may be, in KB. external_links true or false false Accepted, but bearings 0.1 does not read it: external links are checked only when you run rake docs:check:external.

title: The manifest
heading: When the manifest is wrong
text: A manifest that can’t be read stops the build before anything is written. Every problem in it is reported at once, as a manifest problem on the line it is on: Message What it means was not found There is no file at the manifest’s path. the manifest is empty The file has no YAML in it. the manifest is not valid YAML The YAML parser’s own message follows. the manifest holds only text, numbers, true or false, lists and mappings A date, a :symbol, a YAML tag or an alias. Quote a date or a symbol to make it text. … must be a mapping The manifest, site, outputs, checks, a group or a page is not a mapping. … is missing key A required key is missing, or has no value. … has an unknown key key A key the manifest, site, outputs or checks doesn’t take. The hint lists the ones it does. key must be … A value of the wrong kind, such as a list where text belongs. slug slug is not URL-safe A slug with a capital, a space, a leading / or another character outside the allowed ones. duplicate slug slug, first used on line n Two pages share a slug. duplicate source source, first used on line n Two pages share a guide.

title: The layout
text: bearings has no theme and never will. The look of a site belongs to the repo that builds it, in a few files beside the manifest: File What it is layout.html.erb The template every guide is rendered through. Required. index.html.erb The template for the landing page, /index.html. Required. anything else Copied into the site as it is, at the same path, hidden files (names starting with .) excepted: stylesheets, scripts, fonts, icons, a 404.html, a CNAME. If either template is missing, the build reports a layout problem, was not found, and writes no HTML pages and none of the files beside the templates; the other outputs are still written.

title: The layout
heading: How the templates run
text: Both are ERB, with - trimming: a line that starts with <%- and ends with -%> leaves nothing behind, so a loop leaves no blank lines. Nothing is escaped for you. <%= %> writes a value exactly as it is, which is what body needs, since it is HTML. Titles and descriptions come from your own guides and manifest; if one may hold a < or an &, escape it with ERB::Util.h. A template is Ruby, so a mistake in one raises when it runs. rake docs:serve prints the error and keeps serving the last good site.

title: The layout
heading: What both templates get
text: Name What it is site The manifest’s site block: site.name, site.summary, site.url, site.repo, site.version (the version file’s path) and site.namespaces. A key the manifest leaves out is nil, or an empty list for namespaces. version The version read from the file site.version names, such as '1.2.0', or nil without one. groups The groups, in manifest order. Each has a label, its pages in order, and extras. pages Every page, in reading order.

title: The layout
heading: What the layout gets as well
text: Name What it is page The page being rendered. body The guide as HTML, without its # title line, which the layout shows from page.title. toc One { id:, title: } hash for each ## heading in the body, in order. The title is the heading’s HTML with its tags removed. prev_page The page before this one in reading order, or nil on the first. next_page The page after this one, or nil on the last. search_index_url /search.json, the search index, for a layout that offers search.

title: The layout
heading: A page
text: Field What it is title The text of the guide’s first # line. description The page’s description from the manifest. slug The page’s slug from the manifest. url /guides/<slug>/. markdown_url /guides/<slug>.md, the page’s markdown copy. canonical_url The page’s full URL under site.url, or nil without one. edit_url The guide’s edit link under site.repo, or nil without one. source_path The guide’s path from the repo root. group_label The label of the page’s group. num The page’s two-digit number, such as '03'; The manifest says how it counts. featured The page’s featured flag from the manifest. extras The page’s other keys from the manifest, as a hash with string keys. diagrams? Whether the guide has a Mermaid diagram, so the layout loads Mermaid only where it is needed. Pages are compared by value, so p == page picks out the current page in a loop over pages.

title: The layout
heading: What the body holds
text: The body is kramdown’s HTML for the guide, read as GitHub-flavoured markdown, with these changes: A link to another guide, such as [the checks](CHECKS.md#redirect), points at that guide’s page, /guides/checks/#redirect. A link to a markdown file that is not a page is reported as a link problem. Every heading has an id, made the way GitHub makes them, so a link to a heading works in both places. Code blocks in a language Rouge highlights are a div with the classes language-<name> highlighter-rouge, holding a div class="highlight" and then a pre class="highlight"; a block with no language, a text or plaintext one, or one Rouge doesn’t know is a bare pre holding a code (with the class language-<name> when it names a language), so a layout styles both shapes. The tokens are spans with Rouge’s short class names. The layout’s stylesheet colours them; rougify style github prints one such stylesheet. An alert block, a quote that starts with [!NOTE], [!TIP], [!IMPORTANT], [!WARNING] or [!CAUTION], becomes a div with the classes alert alert-note (or -tip, and so on), holding a p class="alert-title" with the kind’s name and then the quote’s text. A Mermaid diagram becomes a pre class="mermaid" holding its source, and an image points at its copy under /assets/; Diagrams and images covers both. The body holds only structure and class names. How an alert or a code block looks is the stylesheet’s job.

title: The layout
heading: The landing page
text: index.html.erb becomes /index.html. It gets site, version, groups and pages, but no page or body: it is not a guide. A landing page usually says what the project is and lists the guides with their descriptions.

title: The layout
heading: The files beside them
text: Every other file in the manifest’s folder, in any subfolder, except hidden files (names starting with .), is copied into the site at the same path: docs-site/site.css is served at /site.css, docs-site/fonts/body.woff2 at /fonts/body.woff2. Point at them from the templates by those paths. A 404.html is worth adding: rake docs:serve answers a path the site doesn’t have with it, and GitHub Pages does the same.

title: The layout
heading: bearings’ own layout
text: bearings builds its own site from these guides, with a plain layout written as a working example: layout.html.erb, index.html.erb and site.css. It is not a theme, and the gem does not ship it: copy what is useful.

title: Diagrams and images
text: A guide shows a diagram or an image the way GitHub expects: a Mermaid fence, or an image with a path relative to the guide. bearings keeps both working on the site, and checks them.

title: Diagrams and images
heading: Mermaid diagrams
text:
Write a diagram as a fenced code block with the language mermaid. Mermaid is text, so an agent can write it and read it back, a change to it is an ordinary diff, and GitHub draws it in place: ```mermaid flowchart LR accTitle: From guide to site guide["a guide"] --> site["the site"] ``` On the site, the fence becomes a pre with the class mermaid, holding the diagram’s source, escaped as HTML: 
flowchart LR accTitle: From guide to site guide["a guide"] --> site["the site"]
The markdown copy keeps the fence as written, so an agent reads the source.

title: Diagrams and images
heading: Drawing them in the browser
text: Turning the source into a picture is the layout’s job, which keeps bearings free of Node and of any one Mermaid version. A layout loads Mermaid on the pages that need it, which page.diagrams? tells it: <%- if page.diagrams? -%> <script type="module"> import mermaid from "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/mermaid@11/dist/mermaid.esm.min.mjs"; mermaid.initialize({ startOnLoad: true }); </script> <%- end -%> Mermaid finds every pre class="mermaid" on the page and draws it. Getting started has a diagram drawn this way.

title: Diagrams and images
heading: What is checked
text: rake docs:check reports a diagram that is empty, one whose first line names no Mermaid diagram type, and one with no accTitle: line. The accTitle is the diagram’s alt text: what a screen reader announces in place of the picture. Add an accDescr: line too when the title alone doesn’t say what the diagram shows. The check doesn’t run Mermaid, so a mistake further into a diagram is not reported: look at the page in rake docs:serve after changing one.

title: Diagrams and images
heading: Images
text: Show an image with markdown, or with an HTML img, or a picture whose sources give other versions. Its path is relative to the guide, as GitHub reads it: ![The bearings mark: a compass needle inside a ring](images/bearings.svg) That line, in this guide, shows this: For every image a guide shows, bearings: copies the file into the site under /assets/, at its path from the repo root, so docs/images/bearings.svg is served at /assets/docs/images/bearings.svg; points the page’s src or srcset at that copy; adds width and height, read from the file, to an img that sets neither, so the page doesn’t shift as it loads (it reads them from PNG, GIF and JPEG files, and from an SVG’s width and height or its viewBox); adds loading="lazy" to an img that doesn’t set loading; points the markdown copy at the image’s full URL under site.url, so the copy shows it when read on its own. An image path that starts with / or names another site is left as it is. Keep images next to the guides, in a folder the manifest watches, so the check can tell you when one is no longer used.

title: Diagrams and images
heading: What is checked
text: rake docs:check reports an image with no alt text, one that is not there, one larger than the manifest’s checks.image_limit_kb (300 KB unless you set it), and one in a watched folder that no guide shows. Alt text is all an agent or a screen reader gets, so write it as a description of what the image shows, not as its name. An image loaded from another site is a warning: it breaks when you read the guides offline, and it can change or vanish without a diff. The checks lists every image problem.

title: The outputs
text: Every build writes the whole site into _site/ at the repo root. Each output is made from the manifest, the guides and the images they show, the templates and the files beside them, and nothing else, so the same sources always build the same site. Path What it is Written when index.html The landing page, from index.html.erb both templates are there guides/<slug>/index.html Each guide, through layout.html.erb both templates are there guides/<slug>.md Each guide’s markdown copy always assets/<path> Each image a guide shows, at its path from the repo root always any other path Each other file beside the manifest, except hidden ones, at the same path both templates are there llms.txt The index of the guides for agents site.url is set llms-full.txt Every guide’s markdown copy in one file outputs.llms_full is true sitemap.xml and robots.txt The page list for search engines site.url is set <old path>/index.html A redirect stub for each of the manifest’s redirects always search.json The search index always A build deletes any file in _site/ it did not write this time, and any folder left empty, so _site/ always holds exactly one build. If two outputs would write the same path, such as a redirect stub and a file copied from beside the manifest, the build reports an output problem and writes nothing.

title: The outputs
heading: HTML pages
text: Each guide is rendered through the layout at /guides/<slug>/, and the landing page at /. The layout is the contract for both: what each template is given and what the body holds.

title: The outputs
heading: Markdown copies
text: Each guide is also written as markdown, at /guides/<slug>.md, for agents and for anyone who would rather read the source. A copy is the guide as written, with two kinds of change: A link to another guide points at that guide’s copy, keeping its #fragment: [the checks](CHECKS.md#image) becomes [the checks](/guides/checks.md#image). An image points at its copy on the site: its full URL under site.url, or its /assets/ path without one. Everything else is kept byte for byte, including code blocks, code spans, alert blocks and Mermaid fences. A link-shaped string inside a code span or a code block is left alone.

title: The outputs
heading: llms.txt
text: /llms.txt tells an agent what documentation exists and where to read it as markdown. It is generated from the manifest, so it can’t drift from the guides: # bearings > A themeless docs engine: plain markdown guides in, a checked static site and llms.txt out. ## Start here - [Getting started](https://bearings.bottrall.dev/guides/getting-started.md): Install bearings, add the two Rakefile lines and build a first site It has site.name as its title, site.summary quoted beneath, and a section for each group, listing each page’s title, the full URL of its markdown copy and its description. Without a site.url it can’t give full URLs, so it is not written, and the build reports an llms warning. With outputs.llms_full: true, /llms-full.txt holds every guide’s markdown copy, in reading order, each ending in a newline and separated from the next by a blank line. It needs no site.url.

title: The outputs
heading: search.json
text: /search.json is the data for a search box in the layout. bearings writes the index and nothing else: the search box and its script are the layout’s. It is a JSON array with an entry for each section of each page, in reading order. Here is one entry, with its text cut short: [ { "title": "The outputs", "heading": "search.json", "text": "/search.json is the data for a search box in the layout.", "url": "/guides/outputs/#searchjson" } ] Field What it is title The page’s title. heading The section’s heading, or null for the text before a page’s first heading. text The section’s text, with the markup removed and the whitespace collapsed. Code blocks are included. url The section’s URL, with the heading’s id as its fragment; the page’s URL for the text before it. Any heading, of any level, starts a new section. The layout is given the index’s path as search_index_url.

title: The outputs
heading: sitemap.xml and robots.txt
text: /sitemap.xml lists the site’s root URL and each page’s canonical URL, in reading order. /robots.txt allows everything and points at the sitemap: User-agent: * Allow: / Sitemap: https://bearings.bottrall.dev/sitemap.xml Both need full URLs, so without a site.url neither is written, and the build reports a sitemap warning.

title: The outputs
heading: Redirect stubs
text: Each of the manifest’s redirects writes a small HTML page at the old path, /guides/setup/ writing guides/setup/index.html. The page sends the browser on to the new path at once, with a refresh meta tag, names the new path’s full URL under site.url (or the path itself, without one) as its canonical link, and links to it for anyone whose browser doesn’t follow the refresh. rake docs:check reports a redirect that points nowhere, one that points at another redirect, and one that would replace a page; The checks has the details.

title: The outputs
heading: Images
text: Each image a guide shows is copied to /assets/<path>, where <path> is its path from the repo root. Diagrams and images covers what else is done to an image on its way into a page.

title: The checks
text: If rake docs:check passes, the site is correct: every guide is listed, every link and anchor resolves in every output, every example parses, every constant a guide names exists, and every image and diagram is there and described. When it fails, each problem names the markdown source and line to fix. A run reports every problem it finds, from every step it could reach, and exits with status 1 if any of them is an error. A warning is printed but doesn’t fail the run. Important No check can be turned off. A check that raises a false alarm is a bug in bearings: report it, rather than working around it in the guide.

title: The checks
heading: Reading a report
text: Each problem is printed with its file, its line, the check that found it, what is wrong, and a hint on the line below. They are sorted by file, then line: docs/GUIDE.md:12: [image] shows an image with no alt text describe the image in its alt text; it is all an agent or a screen reader gets docs/GUIDE.md:30: [anchor] links to `#instal`, but guides/guide/index.html has no id `instal` point the fragment at an id on that page, such as a heading's With FORMAT=json, the same problems are printed as one JSON array, [] when there are none: [ { "check": "image", "level": "error", "file": "docs/GUIDE.md", "line": 12, "message": "shows an image with no alt text", "hint": "describe the image in its alt text; it is all an agent or a screen reader gets" } ] level is error or warning, and hint may be null.

title: The checks
heading: Problems in every build
text: These come from building the site, so rake docs and rake docs:serve report them too: Check Level Message What to do manifest error was not found, or a problem in the manifest When the manifest is wrong lists them all layout error was not found Add layout.html.erb and index.html.erb beside the manifest source error is listed in the manifest but was not found Add the guide, or remove its page from the manifest title error has no “# “ title line Start the guide with a # Title line version error has no version Set VERSION = '…' in the file, or point site.version at the one that does link error links to FILE.md, which is not a page Point the link at a guide the manifest lists, or list that guide llms warning has no site.url, so llms.txt was not written Set site.url sitemap warning has no site.url, so sitemap.xml and robots.txt were not written Set site.url output error n output files have this path Give each output its own path A guide may link to any markdown file GitHub can show, but on the site only a guide the manifest lists has a page, so a link to any other markdown file is a link problem. Link to a file outside the guides by its full URL on GitHub instead. The rest of this guide covers the checks only rake docs:check runs.

title: The checks
heading: unlisted and description
text: Every markdown file in a folder the manifest watches must be a page, and every page needs a description. Check Level Message unlisted error is in a watched folder but no page in the manifest lists it description error has no description in the manifest

title: The checks
heading: code
text: Every fenced ruby, json and yaml block in a guide must parse: Ruby with Prism, JSON with Ruby’s JSON parser, and YAML with Psych, which accepts any valid YAML, aliases and dates included. A block in any other language is not checked, nor is an indented one. Check Level Message code error the ruby example does not parse: what the parser reported The line is the line of the error, not of the fence. Show code you left out as a comment, not as ..., which is seldom valid where it stands.

title: The checks
heading: constant
text: With site.namespaces set, every constant under those namespaces that a guide names must be declared in the repo’s RBS signatures, in sig/. A renamed or deleted class is then a failing check rather than a stale guide. The check reads every fenced ruby block and every inline code span, as Ruby, so `MyGem::Client.new` in a sentence counts as naming MyGem::Client. Only names under a listed namespace are checked, the namespace itself included; a constant a ruby block on the same page defines counts as declared. It needs the rbs gem, and without site.namespaces it doesn’t run. Check Level Message constant error names MyGem::Clinet, which the RBS signatures do not declare The hint suggests the closest declared name, if one is close.

title: The checks
heading: diagram
text: Every Mermaid diagram must have a type and a title. Diagrams and images explains why. Check Level Message diagram error has an empty diagram diagram error has a diagram whose first line names no Mermaid diagram type diagram warning has a diagram with no accTitle line, the alt text that describes it The first line may come after Mermaid front matter and %% comment lines, as Mermaid allows.

title: The checks
heading: image
text: Every image a guide shows must be there, described and small enough, and every image in a watched folder must be shown. Check Level Message image error shows an image with no alt text image error shows images/flow.png, which was not found image error shows images/flow.png, which is 412 KB, over the 300 KB limit image warning loads https://example.com/flow.png from another site image error is in a watched folder but no guide shows it The limit is the manifest’s checks.image_limit_kb. In a watched folder, a file is an image if it ends in .avif, .gif, .jpeg, .jpg, .png, .svg or .webp.

title: The checks
heading: redirect
text: Each of the manifest’s redirects must lead somewhere. Each problem is reported on the redirect’s line in the manifest. Check Level Message redirect error redirect from /old/ would replace a page of the site redirect error redirect from /old/ points to /new/, another redirect redirect error redirect from /old/ points to /new/, which is not a page or file in the site For a redirect to another redirect, the hint names the path to point at instead.

title: The checks
heading: link and anchor
text: Every internal link in every output must lead to a file the site writes, and every #fragment in an HTML page must name an id on the page it points at. The check reads: each guide’s HTML page, including the links the layout adds; each guide’s markdown copy; the landing page; llms.txt. A link with a scheme, such as https: or mailto:, or one starting with //, is external and not checked here. A full URL under site.url is internal and checked like any other. A link shown as code is text, not a link. Check Level Message link error links to /guides/gone/, which is not a file in the site link error its copy guides/start.md links to /gone.md, which is not a file in the site anchor error links to /guides/start/#instal, but guides/start/index.html has no id instal Each problem points at the line it was written on: the guide’s line for a link in a guide, line 1 of layout.html.erb for a link the layout adds, of index.html.erb for one on the landing page, and of the manifest for one in llms.txt.

title: The checks
heading: The README’s links
text: When the repo has a README.md, its relative links must lead to files in the repo, and its anchors to headings that exist: one of its own, or one on the page of a guide it links to. These are reported in README.md as link and anchor problems: Check Level Message link error links to docs/GONE.md, which is not a file in the repo anchor error links to LICENSE#terms, an anchor in a file that is not a guide anchor error links to docs/START.md#instal, but guides/start/index.html has no id instal

title: The checks
heading: External links
text: rake docs:check never makes a network request. rake docs:check:external is the check that does: it requests every http and https link in the guides, each distinct URL once, following up to five redirects and waiting up to ten seconds for each. Check Level Message external-links error https://example.com/gone returned HTTP 404 external-links error https://example.com/ could not be fetched: why it failed external-links warning https://example.com/ could not be fetched: timed out after 10s A timeout is only a warning, since the site may just be slow. Run it now and then, or on a schedule, rather than on every change: a site that is down for a minute shouldn’t fail a build.
